title.narrative: Strengthening Governance for Improved Service Delivery Program (Subprogram 1)

description.narrative: The Governance for Improved Service Delivery program is a key component of ADB's support to the Government of Cambodia on meeting is public finance reform agenda to support improved economic and social outcomes in the country. The program is aligned to the government's recently released Pentagonal Strategy Phase I, 2024-2028 outlining government's reform vision for development outcomes. Under ADB's country partnership strategy for Cambodia, 2024-2028, the program is aligned with the cross cutting goal of improved governance and institutional capacity and also strategic pillar 2 on advancing human development, specifically targeting improvements on service delivery. The program will contribute to following four operational priorities of ADB's Strategy 2030: (i) addressing remaining poverty and reducing inequalities; (ii) accelerating progress in gender equality; (iii) tackling climate change, building climate and disaster resilience, and enhancing environmental sustainability; and (iv) strengthening governance and institutional capacity. Subprogram 1 is aligned with the Paris Agreement by strengthening PFM systems for improved climate planning and resilience at both the national and local level, the latter often being first line responders to disasters.

Policy Action/s as listed by the project staff.

Reform area: Improved performance-based systems and public service delivery
Outcome: All domestically funded public investment projects reflected in FMIS
Description: The Ministry of Economy and Finance signed performance agreements with all sector line ministries for aligning budgets to the delivery of effective and efficient public services, thereby promoting greater accountability, improving resource prioritization, and driving measurable improvements in service quality across sectors. (GDB, MEF, line ministries)

Reform area: Improved performance-based systems and public service delivery
Outcome: All domestically funded public investment projects reflected in FMIS
Description: The government (i) introduced standard operating procedures for competitive hiring of civil servants to ensure merit, transparency and efficiency in the bureaucracy; (ii) issued a Strategic Plan to increase the number of women in management positions in subnational administrations (2024-2028); and (iii) established qualifications, roles, and responsibilities for PFM staff at national and subnational levels to improve capacity and efficiency of public financial management, which in turn supports strengthening of PFM workforces, and effective use of public funds. (MCS, NCDD)

Reform area: Improved performance-based systems and public service delivery
Outcome: All domestically funded public investment projects reflected in FMIS
Description: The government (i) published the Medium-Term Fiscal Framework (2025-2027) for the first time to increase fiscal transparency; (ii) introduced a policy of annual spending reviews to identify expenditure savings in an effort to improve allocative efficiency of the national budget; and (iii) approved the updated Budget Systems Reform Strategy to outline critical steps in for budgeting in line with phase IV of the PFMRP, thereby strengthening fiscal discipline, accountability, and strategic resource management. (GDB)

Reform area: Improved performance-based systems and public service delivery
Outcome: All domestically funded public investment projects reflected in FMIS
Description: The government expanded the functional use of FMIS and has (i)completed the roll out of the budgetary planning module to all line ministries (with the module to the 14 final line ministries being rolled out in the first half of 2025); (ii) drafted guidelines for the implementation of the budget negotiations through FMIS, to be piloted in two line ministries (MEF and MOE); and (iii) piloted the FMIS system for domestically funded public investments in two line ministries (MORD and MOPWT). (GDB, GDPFMIT)

Reform area: Improved performance-based systems and public service delivery
Outcome: All domestically funded public investment projects reflected in FMIS
Description: The government operationalized the digitalized one-window service for nine public services in five municipalities, 2 districts, and two khans increasing the efficiency of local public service delivery and improving citizen convenience at the local government levels. (MOI)

Reform area: Improved performance-based systems and public service delivery
Outcome: All domestically funded public investment projects reflected in FMIS
Description: The government will (i) expand the digitalized one-window services at least 10 additional SNAs, boosting efficiency in public service delivery and citizen's interactions with the local governments; and (ii) issue inter-ministerial Prakas detailing guidelines for the use of digitalized services across the SNAs. (MOI)

Reform area: Improved performance-based systems and public service delivery
Outcome: All domestically funded public investment projects reflected in FMIS
Description: The government will (i) issue FMIS blueprint for expanding the coverage of FMIS to other functions, (ii) streamline the FMIS processes for the recurrent budget for all line ministries, (iii) roll out the budgetary negotiation sub-module to another five-line ministries, and (iv) expand the FMIS system for domestically funded public investments to an additional four line ministries. (GDB, GDPFMIT)

Reform area: Improved performance-based systems and public service delivery
Outcome: All domestically funded public investment projects reflected in FMIS
Description: The government will (i) issue the second phase of the budget systems reform strategy for local governments (2026-2030) to improve budget systems at the local government particularly to strengthen budget and policy linkages at SNA level (GDSNAF); (ii) issue of capital expenditure budget ceilings line ministries to capture 100% of the capital expenditure budget; and (iii) update its program budget classification to have programs and subprograms reflect wages and salary budgets and public investment budgets by programs and subprograms. (GDB)

Reform area: Improved performance-based systems and public service delivery
Outcome: All domestically funded public investment projects reflected in FMIS
Description: The government will issue regulations (i) establishing processes, roles and responsibilities for monitoring and evaluating KPIs agreed in the performance agreements with line ministries; and (ii) outlining processes to incorporate performance monitoring part of the annual budget preparation cycle. (MEF, GDB)

Reform area: Improved performance-based systems and public service delivery
Outcome: All domestically funded public investment projects reflected in FMIS
Description: The government will mandate a PFM certification for public finance staff at the district/municipal level that oversee and manage the PFM processes decentralized by the new Financial Regime and Property Management for Sub-National Administrations Law. (MEF, MCS)

Reform area: Strengthened public investment management, especially for climate resilience and private sector participation
Outcome: At least 60% of PIM proposals in 2027 follow the newly introduced eight phase process stipulated under the GGPIM (ensuring climate resilient public investment) for submission to MEF to meet project preparation milestones from feasibility studies to project approvals
Description: The government (i) established and operationalized a window of Project Development Facility for externally financed projects to help in quicker project initialization (GDICDM) and (ii) launched the digital SARMIS to improve the recording and management of state assets, thereby improving asset utilization, reducing losses, and strengthening public sector financial management. (GDSNAF, GDSPNTR, MEF)

Reform area: Strengthened public investment management, especially for climate resilience and private sector participation
Outcome: At least 60% of PIM proposals in 2027 follow the newly introduced eight phase process stipulated under the GGPIM (ensuring climate resilient public investment) for submission to MEF to meet project preparation milestones from feasibility studies to project approvals
Description: The government (i) established the VGF to enhance the use of PPP modality for public investment; (ii) issued fiscal management guidelines for better management of fiscal risks from PPP projects; and (iii) notified priority sectors for the timeframe 2025-2035 (transport and logistics, energy, water and waste management) for which PPP projects will be developed to accelerate infrastructure delivery, promote economic growth, and improve public service quality. (GDPPP, MEF)

Reform area: Strengthened public investment management, especially for climate resilience and private sector participation
Outcome: At least 60% of PIM proposals in 2027 follow the newly introduced eight phase process stipulated under the GGPIM (ensuring climate resilient public investment) for submission to MEF to meet project preparation milestones from feasibility studies to project approvals
Description: The government issued regulations to: (i) delegate greater authority to subnational administrations on procurement by increasing the ceiling amount under which SNAs can take procurement decisions (ii) incentivize greater adherence to reporting and compliance of procurement processes at the local level; and (iii) deconcentrate appropriate budget allocating, and decision-making powers to the lower tiers of government, in line with the Public Procurement law. Reform area: Strengthened public investment management, especially for climate resilience and private sector participation

Reform area: Improved operational efficiency in revenue and expenditure management
Outcome: Non-tax revenues comprise 1.7% of GDP by 2027
Description: The government (i) established clearly defined principles and guidelines for public financial management, aligned to the 2023 PFSL, for all line ministries and budget entities, through the issuance of a comprehensive PFMM; and (ii) published for the first time cash-based IPSAS financial statements for 2023, marking a significant step toward improved fiscal reporting, and better-informed decision-making in public resource management (GDB, GDNT).

Reform area: Improved operational efficiency in revenue and expenditure management
Outcome: Non-tax revenues comprise 1.7% of GDP by 2027
Description: The government (i) set more robust procedures for budget execution and control as well as public accounting operations to ensure the efficiency, effectiveness, transparency and accountability of public financial management; (ii) issued guidelines on budget execution for line ministries; (iii) established BCUs in line ministries to improve budget execution; and (iv) defined the roles of budget controllers to review, execute, and monitor budgets across line ministries and provincial/capital government authorities, ensuring compliance with regulations and enhancing the efficiency, effectiveness, and accountability of public spending, which contributes to improved service delivery outcomes through more strategic and transparent use of public resources. (GDB, GDNT)

Reform area: Improved operational efficiency in revenue and expenditure management
Outcome: Non-tax revenues comprise 1.7% of GDP by 2027
Description: The government issued guiding regulations to decentralize revenue collection functions (taxpayer services, penalties, and management of state properties), from national to subnational level to boost efficiency of collection and sustainable financing of services delegated to the subnational level, thereby strengthening local fiscal autonomy, improving service delivery responsiveness, and enhancing accountability at the local level. (GDSNAF)

Reform area: Improved operational efficiency in revenue and expenditure management
Outcome: Non-tax revenues comprise 1.7% of GDP by 2027
Description: The government issued the Revenue Mobilization Strategy, Phase 3 2024-2028, providing a comprehensive medium-term framework for strengthening tax administration and tax policy measures, including a clear path for reducing tax expenditures in the medium-term to provide additional fiscal space for improved public services. (MEF, GDP)

Reform area: Improved operational efficiency in revenue and expenditure management
Outcome: Non-tax revenues comprise 1.7% of GDP by 2027
Description: The government will (i) implement CGT mandating a rate of 20% tax applied to profits from the sale or transfer of capital in all defined asset categories; (ii) implement the law on Personal Income Tax, to strengthen revenue mobilization efforts and ensure fair and sustainable financing of reforms; and (iii) submit the Public Debt Management law to the National Assembly. (MEF, GDP, GDT, GDICDM)

Reform area: Improved operational efficiency in revenue and expenditure management
Outcome: Non-tax revenues comprise 1.7% of GDP by 2027
Description: The government will issue customized FMMs, prepared by individual line ministries in collaboration with MEF under the PFMM framework, to detail sector specific PFM practices and budget cycle arrangements including budget planning, expenditure management, monitoring, and audit, aligned to the Public Finance System Law. (GSC, PFM Reform Committee)

Reform area: Improved operational efficiency in revenue and expenditure management
Outcome: Non-tax revenues comprise 1.7% of GDP by 2027
Description: The government will operationalize its Non-Tax Revenue Information Management system, a web-based portal system to provide accurate and timely non-tax revenue data for policymakers in budget entities at the national and subnational level. (GDSNAF, GDSPNTR)
